_about: Generated by scripts/build_accuracy.py from pass-a.json, pass-b.json and the notes-recheck files (evidenceline.verification); do not edit by hand. Independent automated passes, not a review by a practitioner.

passes.independence: Checked from primary sources only. The compiled criteria notes and the other verification pass were not read.
passes.method: Each value in guidelines.json and fds01_site/soil_criteria.json was compared with the primary source text. NEMP 3.0: the official DCCEEW PDF, fetched from its Wayback Machine capture of 15 March 2025 (dcceew.gov.au times out from this machine), text extracted page by page with pypdf 6.19.0, so PDF and printed pages are exact. ASC NEPM Schedule B1: PDF downloaded directly from legislation.gov.au and extracted with pypdf. NEMP 3.1: a text rendering of the official DCCEEW PDF through the r.jina.ai reader, because direct download and WebFetch both timed out and no archive copy exists; printed pages read from running headers (see caveat). ADWG PFAS fact sheet, ADWG table of updates and the WA Environment WAtch PFAS page: HTML downloaded directly and converted to text. Quotes are verbatim from the extracted text; ' / ' marks a line or cell break inside a table and '...' marks skipped text.

passes.independence: Independent of pass A: this pass did not read the other verification pass or the research notes the data files were copied from.
passes.method: Independent of pass A: this pass did not read the other verification pass or the research notes the data files were copied from. Downloaded each primary source myself on 2026-09-24 (sources list below, with SHA-256 for PDFs) and extracted each PDF page's text with pypdf 6.19.0; HTML pages were reduced to text. Found each table by searching the extracted text, read the row, the column and the footnotes, and recorded both the PDF page (1-based page index in the file) and the printed page (the number in the running header). Quotes are verbatim from the extracted text with runs of whitespace collapsed to one space. Extraction artefacts are kept as they are, for example 'NHMRC 201 1' for 'NHMRC 2011' and '1' superscripts run into column headings ('Residential1 A'). Verdict rules: 'confirmed' only when value, unit, scenario, document, table and page all match; any wrong table or page is a 'mismatch' even if the number is right; 'could_not_verify' when the source could not be reached or does not state the point. Notes are judged separately in note_check and do not change the value verdict. Two en dashes in the WA page quote are written as [dash], because Evidenceline text carries no en or em dashes; no other character in any quote is changed. The script asserts that every quote is present in the extracted source text and that every value in the data files equals the value read from the source.

rechecks.method: Downloaded both primary sources afresh on 2026-09-24 and compared them with the repository files. PFAS NEMP 3.0: the dcceew.gov.au host timed out after 60 seconds, so the pinned Wayback capture of the official file was used (10,682,963 bytes, SHA-256 abcc5c28177e2a96747e292e991ae46dd3d8a0099b3ca80e1750192411ce196e, the same file the corpus manifest records; PDF metadata: title 'PFAS National Environmental Management Plan version 3.0', author 'Heads of EPA Australia and New Zealand', created 3 March 2025). ASC NEPM Schedule B1: downloaded directly from legislation.gov.au (2,615,692 bytes, SHA-256 17788fb3339c5163139dc72cf67234b2276de9115d272ae7770f36c4bd77ad99, footer 'Federal Register of Legislative Instruments F2013C00288'). Text was extracted with pdfplumber and the table pages were also rendered to images and read by eye to confirm footnote markers and superscripts. Quotes below are copied from the extracted text and checked against the rendered page; line breaks are joined with a space. The server wording was read from src/evidenceline/server.py, and core.lookup_limit was run for PFOS, PFHxS and PFOS+PFHxS under 'nemp-3.0' to see what the tool actually returns. This pass did not read the other re-check or the earlier pass files. It is an automated check, not a review by a practitioner.

Independent re-check. Only the repository's current data files, server.py and the primary source PDFs were read; the other re-check and the earlier pass files were not opened. Both PDFs were downloaded fresh on 2026-09-24 and their SHA-256 compared with corpus_manifest.json. Text was taken from each page with pypdf 6.19.0 and read in full around each table, including every footnote. The official DCCEEW address for NEMP 3.0 timed out twice (60 s and 90 s, with and without browser headers), so the 15 March 2025 Wayback Machine capture of that same file was used. Each note was compared word by word with the source; a note passes only if every statement in it is in the source, with nothing added that the source does not say.

notes_not_confirmed.label: PFOS and PFHxS added together, drinking water, PFAS NEMP 3.0
notes_not_confirmed.file_note: Applies to PFOS on its own, PFHxS on its own, and the sum of the two (Table 4, footnote a). Compare each of the three with 0.07 ug/L.
notes_not_confirmed.checked_note: Add PFOS and PFHxS together and compare the total with 0.07 ug/L. This rule has no separate value for PFOS or PFHxS on its own.

A.note: Value 0.07 ug/L, unit, drinking-water scenario, Table 4 and PDF page 57 (printed page 48) are all confirmed. The mismatch is in the note. Footnote a of Table 4 says the sum criterion means 'PFOS only, PFHxS only, and the sum of the two', so 0.07 ug/L also applies to PFOS alone and to PFHxS alone. The note's sentence 'This rule has no separate value for PFOS or PFHxS on its own' contradicts that. When both are measured, passing the sum check means both single checks pass too; but when only one of the two is reported, that one should still be compared with 0.07 ug/L rather than marked as having no value. soil_criteria.json already models the same footnote with each_member_too: true.

B.note: Footnote a to Table 4 says the sum criterion means PFOS only, PFHxS only, and the sum of the two. The note's second sentence ('This rule has no separate value for PFOS or PFHxS on its own') reads as if PFOS or PFHxS alone is not compared with 0.07 ug/L, which is not what the footnote says. The number is right. When both members are measured the sum check also catches either one alone, but when one member is missing or not detected the single member is not screened. Suggested wording: 'Compare PFOS alone, PFHxS alone, and the sum of the two with 0.07 ug/L (Table 4, footnote a).'

recheck_findings.subject: Note next to: Sum of PFOS and PFHxS, soil, HIL A
recheck_findings.first_passes: Both first passes confirmed this note, and it has not changed since.

A.note: soil_criteria.json has no note on the 0.07 ug/L drinking-water value; this is the only note there that touches the same footnote. The NEMP 3.0 half is confirmed: NEMP 3.0 Table 5 footnote a is word for word the same as Table 4 footnote a, and the NEMP 3.0 HIL A value is 0.003 mg/kg for the sum (0.06 mg/kg for PFOA), as the file says. The cited document is NEMP 3.1 (Table 5, printed page 52), which this re-check did not fetch, so the 3.1 footnote and the claim that the value is the same in 3.1 were not checked here.

B.note: The NEMP 3.0 half is confirmed: the NEMP 3.0 Table 5 HIL A value for the sum is 0.003 mg/kg and its footnote a has the wording the note quotes. The file cites NEMP 3.1 Table 5, printed page 52, and says the value is the same in 3.1; the NEMP 3.1 PDF timed out on 2026-09-24 and has no archived copy used here, so the 3.1 side (value, footnote a and page) could not be checked in this re-check.

recheck_findings.subject: The NEMP 3.0 rule in the MCP server's instructions

A.note: Names all three quantities the footnote names and cites the right table and footnote. The capital letters on SUM put more weight on the sum than the footnote does, but the meaning is the same. The next sentence, about the 'current' rule having no sum, is about NEMP 3.1 and was not checked here.

B.note: It names all three quantities the footnote names and the right value and footnote. The capitals on SUM give the sum extra weight, but the sentence goes on to name PFOS alone and PFHxS alone against the same value, so the meaning matches. The sentence about the "current" rule (PFOS and PFHxS separately, no sum) comes from NEMP 3.1 and was not checked here.

A.note: Matches the footnote. Run on 2026-09-24, lookup_limit('PFOS', 'nemp-3.0') and lookup_limit('PFHxS', 'nemp-3.0') both return 0.07 ug/L with a caveat quoting the footnote's words "PFOS only, PFHxS only, and the sum of the two". Only that part of the footnote is quoted, not the whole sentence; that is accurate. 'either' means PFOS or PFHxS, which is clear from the context.

B.note: The statement of what 0.07 ug/L applies to matches the footnote. Checked by running core.lookup_limit for PFOS, PFHxS and PFOS+PFHxS under nemp-3.0: each returns 0.07 ug/L, Table 4, PDF page 57, and the PFOS and PFHxS answers add a caveat quoting "PFOS only, PFHxS only, and the sum of the two". Two small wording points, neither a mismatch with the source: (1) "with the footnote quoted" is true only in part, since the key phrase of footnote a is quoted, not the whole footnote, and only for a PFOS or PFHxS request; (2) the docstring says the result shows "whether it applies to the analyte on its own or to the sum", but for a PFOS or PFHxS request the returned fields read applies_to "sum" and compared_quantity "sum of PFOS and PFHxS", while footnote a says the value applies to that analyte on its own too. The note and caveat in the same result say so correctly; the two fields do not.

recheck_findings.subject: What lookup_limit returns when asked for PFOS or PFHxS under NEMP 3.0

A.note: Under footnote a the value applies to PFOS on its own as well as to the sum. When the caller asked about PFOS, a field that says the compared quantity is the sum points a reader or a model at the sum only, while the note and caveat in the same result say PFOS alone counts too. The note text is right; these two structured fields lag behind it. Suggested change for the owner of core.py (line 129) and models.py: for a member lookup under a rule whose sum value also applies to each member, set compared_quantity to the member on its own, for example 'PFOS on its own (the same value also applies to PFHxS on its own and to the sum)', and either add a third applies_to value such as 'each and sum' or reword the docstring so it no longer promises an either/or answer.

B.note: Not recorded as a separate finding.

recheck_findings.resolution: Fixed after the re-check: for PFOS or PFHxS under NEMP 3.0, the compared quantity now names that analyte on its own, and the tool and field descriptions no longer promise an either/or answer. The verdict shown is about the earlier output.
